correctness.rationale: The definition is reconstructed with the exact unit-sphere and fixed-separation quantifiers. The maps \(R(s,t)=(s-t,s)\) and \(Q(s,t)=(t,s)\) preserve \(N\) and reduce all pairs of hexagon edges to four cyclic separations. For same, adjacent, next-nearest and opposite edge pairs, the proof derives the exact feasible separation and exact minimum of \(N(x+y)\). The only competing minima are \(2-\epsilon/2\) and \(4-2\epsilon\), crossing at \(\epsilon=4/3\). Explicit unit pairs attain each branch for every parameter in its range. The bundled checker replays these identities using exact rational arithmetic.
risks: The checker is a finite replay of the edge formulas; completeness of the continuum argument rests on the explicit symmetry classification proved in RESULT.md.

The affine-regular hexagon is a canonical non-Hilbert normed plane. Its full profile exhibits a sharp chord-type transition at \(\epsilon=4/3\), and the exact value \(\rho_{X_H}^{a}(1)=-1/8\) supplies a concrete benchmark for the source's uniform-non-squareness criterion. The edge-separation classification is reusable for other polyhedral fixed-chord extremal problems.
